steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Carbohydrates are the body's main source of energy. They are divided into sugars (simple, quick-release) and starches (complex, slow-release). Excess glucose is stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles, or converted to fat.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Proteins are essential for growth, repair, and maintenance of body tissues. They are made up of amino acids — there are 20 amino acids, 9 of which are essential (cannot be synthesised by the body and must come from food).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: High biological value (HBV) proteins contain all 9 essential amino acids — found in animal sources (meat, fish, eggs, dairy) and soya. Low biological value (LBV) proteins lack one or more essential amino acids — found in plant sources (cereals, pulses, nuts).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Complementary proteins: combining LBV protein sources to provide all essential amino acids — e.g. rice and beans, hummus and pitta, toast and baked beans.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always give at least two specific food sources for each nutrient Link nutrient functions to health — not just 'energy' but 'provides glucose for brain function' Use the correct terminology: HBV/LBV, essential/non-essential amino acids, saturated/unsaturated
